scope: Center the displayed musical register and preserve trace continuity through short rejected pitch intervals

behavior: The first accepted pitch chooses the nearest staff-centered written octave
Subsequent sustained register changes move the entire note and trace together with the same critically damped spring
The sounding MIDI, true pitch name, pitch filtering and actual melodic intervals remain unchanged
A small 8 or 15 by the clef identifies an octave-transposed display
Rejected pitches cannot change the display register; fixed staff and keyboard-star geometry are unchanged
Missing, low-confidence, out-of-range or unconfirmed frames add no trace samples
Reliable endpoints separated by less than 350ms remain in the same path
A visual-only horizontal tail from the last accepted point reaches the current note while the short-gap window remains open
Longer gaps and true silence, disconnection or session resets start a new segment

additionalChecks: Reference and native rendering preserve octave centering, real pitch names, path continuity, keyboard-star and music layer ordering
Synthetic 800-point light preview and low G2 preview inspected visually
